doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Harlem, Brooklyn and Long Island clubs he worked
summary: He worked Small's, Club Baron, Basie's, Baby Grand, Blue Coronet and others.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Working or looking. When I wasn’t working, I was looking. I met everybody. Everybody you probably can name, I met them.
Wilt Chamberlain bought his interest in Smalls when? 1961? 1962?
Something like that. I don’t know exactly. He had a lot of money.
So you were working for him.
You worked at Smalls. You worked the breakfast thing at Connie’s. Where else did you work in Harlem?
I worked at the Club Barron. I worked at Count Basie’s. He had a club. I worked down at the Baby Grand sometimes. Another place called the Top Club.
About how many days a week would you say you were working from 1955 to the late ‘60s? 300 days a year?
No, not that much. I wouldn’t work that much. There was three or four clubs out in Long Island I worked, too. Bop City and two more clubs out there I used to work.
Yeah, Brooklyn... I used to work the Baby Grand over there, and I used to work Scotty’s Club over there, and that other club on Fulton and Nostrand.
The Blue Coronet. That was a tough club.
Tough in terms of the clientele?
That’s right. You had a few fights now and then.
